title: Asiya and Maryam
hookLine: two women set as examples for all believers: Pharaoh's wife and Maryam (66:11–12)

lines: SHE ASKS FOR A DIFFERENT HOUSE.
cards: Pharaoh's palace. A husband who tells his people he is their lord most high. A wife with everything a palace can give.
And one day she asks for a house. Not a bigger palace. A different house, somewhere else entirely.
The last verses of surah at-Tahrim hold up two women as examples, for everyone who believes, men and women alike. One is the wife of Pharaoh. The other is Maryam.

teach.h: PHARAOH'S WIFE ASKS FOR A HOME.
teach.b: Verse eleven, in Pickthall: "And Allah citeth an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh when she said: My Lord! Build for me a home with Thee in the Garden." It goes on: and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds.
The Qur'an never gives her name; Asiya comes from the hadith.

She's the same woman who, in surah al-Qasas, looked at a baby taken from the river and said: a comfort for me and for you, don't kill him, he may be of use to us. That baby was Musa. Now look at the order of her prayer.
A home with Thee, then in the Garden.
Commentators noticed she asks for the neighbor before the house: near You first, then where. There's an Arabic saying for it, al-jar qabl ad-dar, the neighbor before the house.
Married to Pharaoh, she asked to live near Someone else.
Verse twelve turns to Maryam, daughter of 'Imran: she guarded her chastity, she believed the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and she was among the devout.
Maryam, the mother of 'Isa, is the one woman the Qur'an calls by name, readers note, and a whole surah carries her name.

A hadith in Bukhari says that among women, Maryam and Asiya reached perfection. So the surah ends with one woman inside a tyrant's house and one woman alone, both held up for every believer to learn from.
One had a husband who opposed her faith; the other had no husband at all. The surah holds up the faith of each.

how: Some Muslims memorize and pray Asiya's words from 66:11, asking for a home near Allah in the Garden, and honor her and Maryam among the best of women, as hadith describe them.

o: a queen of Sheba who came to visit Sulayman
Pharaoh's wife, who asked for a home near God
the mother of Musa, who set him in the river

games.q: Asiya and Maryam — tap the pairs.
p: Pharaoh's wife, named in the hadith
mother of 'Isa; a surah bears her name

s: the Qur'an names Pharaoh's wife Asiya
the Qur'an calls her the wife of Pharaoh; the name Asiya comes from hadith.
these two women are examples for men too
the verses set them as an example for all who believe.
Pharaoh's wife is the one who saved baby Musa
in al-Qasas she says: don't kill him, he may be of use to us.

games.q: you're the wife of Pharaoh. you have every comfort a palace can give. you pray. what do you ask for?
o: a home near Allah in the Garden.
games.why: she asked for a home with Allah in the Garden, and to be saved from Pharaoh and his deeds: the neighbor before the house.

practice: If you pray, say her words from the verse slowly, once or a few times: my Lord, build for me a home with Thee in the Garden.
If you don't, think of the place you feel most yourself, and notice what makes it home: the walls, or who is near. Let the house fade and the nearness stay.

wordCard.voice: Asiya. Pharaoh's wife, who asked for a home near Allah before anywhere else, one of two examples, says 66:11–12, for all believers. Today's word.

orig.s: ٱبْنِ لِي عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِي ٱلْجَنَّةِ
orig.note: Arabic, 66:11: build for me, with You, a house in the Garden. 'with You' comes before 'a house'.

carryVoice: Your line: a house near you. Nearness first, then the house itself. See you soon.
